names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 18 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Δαβίδ και Ταριχάνι οι Μάρτυρες», with the rank word left off; the life page carries «Αγιος Ταριχανι ο Μαρτυρας» as its own head name.

The nominative the day page's own `/name/2089.html` link carries in its `title`, «Таричан Грузинский, мч.», with the rank abbreviation left off and the calendar's own epithet of nation kept. The day's own line declines the two together, «Мчч. Давида и Таричана отроков (683) (Груз.).» `fk.mjs` on «Таричан Грузинский» returned NONE before the write, and this is the only folder in the corpus of that name.

death.note: saint.gr: «μαρτύρησαν το 693 μ.Χ., κατά τους χρόνους του Πέρση βασιλέως Αμπντούλ», and its head line reads «Αγιος Ταριχανι ο Μαρτυρας (; - 693)».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 18 мая ст. ст. — «Мчч. Давида и Таричана отроков (683) (Груз.).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day and the same boy, the second of the two Georgian brothers. The calendar marks the entry «(Груз.)» and calls them «отроков», boys. **`dates` were not touched, and the calendar disagrees with itself by ten years**: the notice says they died in 693 at the hands of the Persian governor Абдула for refusing Islam, which is the year this folder already carries, while the day line prints «(683)». Both are the same page's and both are in the life. He already carries his brother as a `related` row. The day page prints no hymn for them. Their life page gives one day only. azbyka.ru was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Δαβίδ και Ταριχάνι οι Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives him as one of two head names on one page — hence two folders. **Nothing in the corpus reads as him**: the name appears in no folder, and the namesweep printed no row for it. **The name is kept in the form the page prints**, Ταριχάνι, and is not regularised to a Georgian or Latin spelling the page never gives; the display name adds only the brother, who is what distinguishes him. **No country is given** and there is no `locations` object. No manner of death, no relics and no hymn is printed.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
